rule.description: One conceptual responsibility - creating the package's falsy identity sentinels - is re-implemented by private machinery in two or more production modules instead of being owned by a single shared implementation. A module carries such machinery when it locally defines a sentinel-shaped type (a class, or a type assembled via type()) whose body provides __bool__ returning constant False together with __repr__ reflecting a stored name/description attribute on self. boltons/typeutils.py, which exposes the canonical shared implementation boltons.typeutils.make_sentinel, is the reference owner and is exempt: a single owner implementing the responsibility is not a scatter. The rule is owner-agnostic for repairs: moving the whole responsibility into any one module leaves at most one non-exempt implementer and passes.

checks.description: Detect modules that ship their own private identity-sentinel machinery (a sentinel-shaped type defined in the module itself) instead of obtaining markers from a single shared owner. Every match is one module re-implementing the same provisioning responsibility; the scattered set of matches together is the shotgun-surgery relation.
checks.detected_relation: module -> private re-implementation of the shared 'provision identity sentinels' responsibility
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A conceptual change to the shared responsibility (marker repr convention, pickle/copy support, registry or validation policy) would require synchronized semantic edits in every listed module, because each module owns a divergent copy of the same machinery.

matches.evidence: Local factory _make_sentinel defines class _Sentinel (slots-based) providing falsy __bool__ and name-based __repr__, bypassing the shared owner.

Local memoizing factory _new_sentinel plus _SENTINEL_CACHE registry defines class _Sentinel with falsy __bool__, name-based __repr__ and __reduce__, duplicating and diverging from the shared owner (registry + pickle policy are local additions).
Module-level class _NoDefaultType defines falsy __bool__ and name-based __repr__ and is instantiated directly as NO_DEFAULT, a private re-implementation of the shared provisioning responsibility.
Local factory _make_sentinel defines class _MissingMarker with falsy __bool__, name-based __repr__ and local __copy__/__deepcopy__ policy, diverging from the shared owner's copy semantics.
Module-level class _UnsetType defines falsy __bool__, name-based __repr__ and __reduce__ pickling policy for the _UNSET trace marker, re-implementing provisioning locally.

measurement.machinery_kind: bare module-level class with pickle policy

matches.evidence: Local factory _make_tombstone validates marker names and defines class _Tombstone with falsy __bool__ and name-based __repr__; the lazy-deletion marker _REMOVED is provisioned privately instead of by the shared owner.
Local factory _make_sentinel defines class _Marker with falsy __bool__ and a class-name-based repr, provisioning both internal remap walkers (_UNSET, _REMAP_EXIT) privately.

Local factory _make_sentinel assembles the marker type dynamically via type() with a method dict defining falsy __bool__ and name-based __repr__, a structurally different but conceptually identical copy of the provisioning responsibility.

Local factory _make_sentinel mirrors the shared owner's two-argument signature and defines class _UnsetMarker with falsy __bool__ and name-based __repr__, provisioning _UNSET privately for every recv/send default.

Module-level class _MissingCellType defines falsy __bool__ and name-based __repr__ and is instantiated directly as the _MISSING marker used by the table constructors, re-implementing provisioning locally.
Local factory _make_sentinel defines class _QueryMarker with falsy __bool__, name-based __repr__ and a description attribute, provisioning the query-parameter marker _MISSING privately.

excluded.reason: Canonical shared owner of the provisioning responsibility (public, documented, tested API). Its machinery is the reference implementation, not a divergent copy; the checker reports it as the exempt owner construct and never counts it as a violation.

A bare `_UNSET = object()` module assignment. It provisions no sentinel-shaped type and defines no marker policy (no bool/repr/copy semantics), so it is not an implementer of the provisioning responsibility and is out of scope for the rule.
A plain `_UNSET = object()` created inside a function body. It defines no machinery and no marker policy, so the rule does not count it; a solver does not need to touch it.
